pr_title: Add new highlighting color for `@GDScript` and `@GlobalScope` functions
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/47644
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/64621

"assert" and "preload" are reserved words, so they get highlighted even without a bracket after. Miscellaneous global functions like `as`, `is`, and `await` remain colored as keywords.

Quite awkward, but GDScript's `get_reserved_words` also adds GDScript's utility functions, although they are not actually reserved, and there's an overlap.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85438892/185738919-96280bbf-1369-4a01-980e-106517f66b56.png)

Feel free to bikeshed the defaults
pr_comments: The chosen color seems good to me. In the end, I think this is a good option to have – if you don't want global scope functions to have a different color, set them to have the same color as functions in the syntax theme.

Very nice! I thought overridden method definitions in a Class should've also had a slightly different hue, since I do keep getting them mixed sometimes, especially when adding my own. And I was also thinking of leaning towards purple since it isn't used anywhere else...

Should open a proposal and try to get some consensus on this IMO @Mickeon 

I'll keep the PR for global funcs only

issue_context.title: `@GDScript` function names are highlighted when they shouldn't
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.alpha14

### System information

Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS

### Issue description

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85438892/185643677-9aeb688d-42c8-4a45-8a6a-bae76ee0f025.png)

This is allowed, although it does send a warning. Other function names do not trigger function highlighting until you add `(` after, even those of `@GlobalScope`, but those of `@GDScript` do.

### Steps to reproduce

Type `var str` in GDScript

### Minimal reproduction project

Too simple to send a project for
comments: Shouldn't global scope function names be reserved keywords anyway?

I dunno, we could decide that this, instead, is the real issue. Global scope functions are not usable as callables, so if they aren't used like functions, there is no collision atm. At least I think so.

They should not be reserved, I don't think. They cannot be passed as callables. But in this case specifically, even if GDScript encourages more explicit variable names, "str" is a fairly common shorthand used during String manipulations.

review_comments: Why do those need special casing here since they were already appended to the HashSet?
> "assert" and "preload" are reserved words, so they get highlighted even without a bracket after
